title: Support Toolchain Orchestrator: lightweight admin CLI and evented runbook fabric
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: On-call engineers frequently perform short, repetitive admin actions (rotate keys, evict stuck jobs, refresh caches, promote fallback models) via ad-hoc scripts and chat instructions. These are hard to discover, poorly instrumented, and risky to run in bursts during incidents. Goal: build a lightweight orchestrator that turns curated runbook steps into composable CLI commands and evented tasks that can run in: (a) interactive mode for SREs, (b) scheduled dry-run for runbook QA, and (c) automated trigger from incident playbooks. The system should integrate with our audit logs, RBAC, and telemetry so every action is attributed and reversible where possible.
acceptance_criteria: A discoverable CLI subcommand 'redwood ops-run' lists curated safe operations with descriptions and required permissions
Operators can execute a runbook step with a --dry-run flag that emits a simulated execution plan and tokenized telemetry event
Each completed run emits an audit log entry with user, runbook id, inputs, and a unique run id that maps to the console trace
We provide a minimal JSON Schema for step inputs and validation at runtime to prevent common footguns
The orchestrator supports scheduled verification runs (nightly dry-runs) that post to the runbook QA dashboard and flag regressions
tasks: Define step manifest format and JSON Schema for inputs/outputs
Implement CLI surface (list, describe, run, dry-run) with pluggable backend handlers
Add audit-event emitter and map run ids to console traces and logs
Wire RBAC checks to existing IAM roles and add gating for high-privilege steps
Create nightly runbook QA job that executes dry-runs and reports regressions to the QA dashboard
Write migration guide and register first 10 canonical admin steps (rotate-key, model-fallback, cache-warm, evict-job, scale-pool)
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose a manifest-first approach (YAML/JSON) instead of hardcoding commands in the CLI to enable non-dev teams to author/run steps
2026-02-28: Decided to use existing audit-log pipeline (kinesis -> datalake) rather than a new silo; requires small producer change to emit run_id metadata
2026-03-05: Opted for lightweight local sandboxing (namespace isolation) for dry-runs rather than full VM sandboxes to keep iteration fast
2026-03-09: Agreed to require security_review for any step that touches KMS or SG-managed secrets (marked in manifest via requires_secrets flag)
risks: Risk: Incorrect input validation could allow unsafe operations — mitigated by strict JSON Schema + preflight checks
Risk: Over-privileging the orchestrator agent — mitigated by RBAC enforcement and step-level permission declarations
Risk: Telemetry volume growth from nightly dry-runs — mitigated by sampling and aggregated QA metrics
Risk: Adoption friction for SREs used to ad-hoc scripts — mitigated by import tooling and one-click onboarding docs
